main_logic: Convective wind is read as pressure ratio: (event 3-second gust / ASCE MRI300 reference design gust, 10 m, Exposure C) squared, valid 0 to 2.

Same station assembly and same direct aerodynamic loading on a squared 3-second gust ratio, so the hurricane GSU/substation curve is reused as a judgment-based cross-hazard proxy for direct wind only.
The damage ratio is a share of the replacement value of the same fenced station, $27,353,236.37 (MISO MTEP24 published table amounts), applied once.

steps.name: What it covers
steps.meaning: The parts that have a curve, their share of the value, and what has none yet
paragraphs: Convective wind on substations: same station assembly and same direct aerodynamic loading on a squared 3-second gust ratio, so the hurricane GSU/substation curve is reused as a judgment-based cross-hazard proxy for direct wind only (see docs/contracts/hazard_handoff/substation_convective_wind_screening_v1/README.md). It names 1 part: Whole station (fenced assembly). Outside its scope: external access road and project support allowances ($3.06M, outside the fenced value), business interruption and service interruption and overlap with Hurricane wind (not deduplicated; a downstream Total decision). Kinds of damage it does not include: tornado-only mechanisms: windborne debris, pressure change, rotation and duration and cascading electrical failures.
For this hazard the substation is split into 1 part: Whole station (fenced assembly).

The damage ratio is a share of replacement value of the same fenced station, $27,353,236.37 (MISO MTEP24 published table amounts), applied once. The files state no plant-level dollar figure for this asset.
